purpose: Compile the exact existing hybrid recipient-envelope computation into private proof wires. No algorithm substitution or public shared-secret output is permitted.

mlkem.license_choice: MIT (upstream offers Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT)
mlkem.source_license: Upstream LICENSE and all source copyright headers must accompany any imported or distributed source and generated artifacts.
mlkem.configuration: ML-KEM-768, portable C, serial FIPS202, deterministic encapsulation; unmodified algorithm source, supported volatile-byte zeroization hook for the assembly-free frontend
mlkem.acceptance: Successful compilation alone is insufficient. Retain unwinding assertions and require their satisfaction, correct key validation and exact cross-implementation ciphertext/shared-secret known answers before admitting a generated circuit.

bearssl.license: MIT, copyright Thomas Pornin; retain LICENSE.txt and source headers
bearssl.purpose: C reference for X25519, HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM only, not a TLS replacement
bearssl.x25519_module_abi: The scoped d-to-OUTPUT_d token rename annotates the destination of f255_mul, f255_square, f255_add, f255_sub and f255_mul_a24 for HyCC's documented pointer module ABI. It changes no core expression. reduce_final_f255 and secret-control cswap remain inline. Native C known-answer bytes remain identical after annotation.

public_known_answers.scope: Nonuniform deterministic seed, recipient, ephemeral public key and shared secret; exact Rust X25519 agreement including seed endianness.
Exact Rust HKDF/AAD/AES-GCM arithmetic agreement only; fixed ct/recipient bytes are not valid KEM objects or evidence of full encapsulation.

status: Integration in progress. No generated encrypted-note relation is accepted yet.
